scope: Proposition 10.1 (Conditional density determines the field) of the manuscript “Uniform excess charge for Coulomb molecules and the outer radius of neutral atoms” (preprints/Uniform-excess-charge-for-Coulomb-molecules-and-the-outer-radius-of-neutral-atoms-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 263 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5abedb3de1f8ed28), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 62. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a universal constant Ccap with the following property. Fix L1 ≥ 2, 0 < hl < hh < ∞, and a sufficiently small ξ > 0; it suffices to require ξ < hl/16. There exists s∗ = s∗(D0, L1, hl, hh, ξ) > 0 such that, whenever 0 < s ≤ s∗, at each j < m, with r = rj, there is an event Gj ∈ Fj satisfying P(Gc j ) ≤ Cr25 on which, simultaneously for r ≤ dy ≤ 4L1r and hl ≤ h ≤ hh, d6 yµj(y) > kh3/2 =⇒ d4 yHj(y) ≥ h − ξ, d6 yµj(y) < kh3/2 =⇒ d4 yHj(y) ≤ h + ξ. (10.5) On the same event, Hj(y) ≤ Ccapd−4 y throughout that band. The constant C may depend on the fixed parameters, whereas Ccap does not depend on D0, L1, hl, hh, ξ. All estimates are uniform in Z, the ground state, j, and m.
